pr_title: Remove unnecessary work from lazy loops (and a little from greedy)
pr_body:
- For a lazy loop, compute whether the child might match empty.  Only if it might do we need any of the checks around empty iterations, and only in those situations do we need to track the starting position or whether we've seen an empty loop, so avoid all work associated with that if the min length of the child is greater than zero.
- If the lazy loop failing will exit the match, avoid doing all the cleanup work that ends up being irrelevant.
- If the lazy loop isn't itself part of another loop, we don't need the backtracking section to push/pop any additional state on the backtracking stack.
- Avoid outputting two gotos in a row in greedy loops.
- Avoid outputting additional if blocks in greedy loops when the checks are identical.
- Add some comments, in particular to loops where the logic can be tricky and hard to follow / reason about.
- Remove some emitted semicolons after labels.
- Fix the naming of a few "SkipBacktrack" labels to conform to the same prefixed naming convention used for other labels

Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/68415

issue_context.title: Improve handling of lazy loops in regex source generator / compiler
issue_context.body:
Lazy loops currently push/pop more state on to the backtracking stack than is generally necessary.  This can be improved.

review_comments:
`string?`
Is the generator not using nullable annotations? If not I suppose we should enable them right?

> Is the generator not using nullable annotations?

It has annotations enabled but warnings disabled.

> If not I suppose we should enable them right?

It targets netstandard2.0, where things like Debug.Assert aren't annotated with [DoesNotReturnWhen(false)], so the number of false positive warnings is staggering.

At one point I temporarily retargeted to .NET 7 and fixed the nullable warnings.  We can do another pass like that.
NIT: the variable name is a bit confusing since it is a `int` as opposed to a `bool`. Should we use something like `laoop_empty_seen_count` or something like that?
It is a Boolean, in that it can only be false (0) or true (1).  It's just stored as an int because that's what our stack stores.
